entry: Extinct genus of radiodont, an order of early-diverging stem-group marine [[Arthropod|arthropods]]. It is best known from *Anomalocaris canadensis*, found in the Stephen Formation (particularly the Burgess Shale) of [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]]. Estimated to reach 34.2–37.8 cm (13.5–14.9 in) long excluding the frontal appendages and tail fan, it is one of the largest animals of the Cambrian and one of the earliest examples of an [[Apex predator|apex predator]]. Its frontal appendages were used to grasp prey.

Eating disorder marked by food restriction, body image disturbance and a fear of gaining weight. Anorexia has one of the highest mortality rates of any psychiatric disorder, second only to opioid overdoses. Medical complications may include [[Osteoporosis]], [[Infertility]], heart damage and death. Treatment restores a healthy weight and addresses underlying psychological problems, often through [[Psychotherapy|talk therapy]].

Annexation of Austria into [[Nazi Germany]] on March 12, 1938. The 1919 Treaty of Saint-Germain and [[Treaty of Versailles]] had forbidden a union of Austria and Germany. Under threat of German invasion, Austrian chancellor Kurt Schuschnigg resigned, and his successor, Arthur Seyss-Inquart, invited German troops into Austria, which entered unopposed. A plebiscite held on April 10, 1938, reported 99.7% approval.

American landscape photographer and environmentalist known for black-and-white images of the American West. He helped found Group f/64, an association advocating “pure” photography with sharp focus and the full tonal range of a print. With Fred Archer he developed the Zone System, a method of achieving a desired final print through control of exposure, negative development and printing. A lifelong conservation advocate, he was first given a camera on a visit to [[Yosemite National Park]] at age 14. He was contracted by the United States Department of the Interior to photograph national parks, and his advocacy helped expand the National Park system; he received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1980. He was a key advisor in founding the photography department at the [[Museum of Modern Art]] in [[New York City]].

Benedictine abbot, philosopher and theologian; archbishop of Canterbury, 1093–1109. As archbishop he defended the Church’s interests in England during the [[Investiture Controversy]], resisting the English kings William II and Henry I, for which he was exiled twice (1097–1100 and 1105–1107). He asserted the primacy of Canterbury over York and the bishops of Wales; [[Pope|Pope Paschal II]] later reversed the papal decisions on the matter. Anselm composed dialogues and treatises combining mystical and rational approaches, and he is regarded as the originator of the ontological argument for the existence of God and of the satisfaction theory of atonement. He was canonized as a [[Saint|saint]] after his death and proclaimed a Doctor of the Church in 1720.

Eusocial [[Insect|insect]] of the family Formicidae, order [[Hymenoptera]]. Ants evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the [[Cretaceous]] period, and more than 13,800 of an estimated 22,000 [[Species|species]] have been described. Colonies range from a few dozen individuals to super colonies that may reach hundreds of millions, and typically include sterile wingless females, most of them workers, along with soldiers and fertile males and queens. Ants have colonized almost every landmass on Earth, except [[Antarctica]] and a few remote or inhospitable islands. They thrive in moist tropical ecosystems and may exceed the combined biomass of wild birds and mammals. Some species are valued as biological pest control agents, while others, such as the red imported [[Fire ant|fire ant]] (*Solenopsis invicta*), are invasive where they have been introduced accidentally.

Brazilian composer and musician, also known as Tom Jobim, and a pioneer of [[Bossa nova|bossa nova]]. He merged [[Samba|samba]] with cool jazz in the 1960s. His song [[The Girl from Ipanema|“Garota de Ipanema”]] has been recorded over 240 times by other artists and is believed to be one of the most recorded popular songs in history. The 1964 album *Getz/Gilberto*, which featured several of his compositions, won [[Grammy Awards]] including Album of the Year, the first jazz record to do so. His 1967 album with [[Frank Sinatra]] was nominated for Album of the Year in 1968.

Portuguese dictator, economist and academic; prime minister of Portugal, 1932–68. After becoming finance minister following the 1926 coup, he balanced the budget and stabilized the currency within a year. He ruled through the corporatist *Estado Novo* (“New State”), which opposed democracy, communism, socialism and liberalism, and used censorship and the PIDE secret police against opposition. He distanced himself from [[Nazism]] and [[Fascism|fascism]]. Portugal became a founding member of [[NATO]] in 1949 and joined the [[United Nations]] in 1955. Salazar supported [[Francisco Franco]] in the [[Spanish Civil War]] and kept Portugal neutral in [[World War II]]. Portugal recorded sustained growth in GDP per capita from the 1950s, yet in 1974 it still had the lowest per capita income and literacy rate in Western Europe. The regime ended with the Carnation Revolution of 1974.

City on the southwest coast of [[Anatolia]], in [[Turkey]], and capital of Antalya Province (urban pop. c. 1.5 million). Founded as Attaleia by King Attalus II of Pergamon, it was conquered by the Romans and retains monuments such as Hadrian’s Gate. It passed to the [[Seljuk Empire]] in 1207 and the [[Ottoman Empire]] in 1391, and was occupied by Italy for three years after [[World War I]] before returning to Turkey during the [[Turkish War of Independence]]. Flanked by the Taurus Mountains, it is Turkey’s largest international sea resort on the Turkish Riviera. In 2023, according to Euromonitor International, it was the fourth-most visited city in the world, with more than 16.5 million foreign visitors.

Capital and largest city of [[Madagascar]], in the central highlands at 1,280 m (4,199 ft) above sea level. It was founded around 1610 by the Merina king Andrianjaka, who built a fortified royal dwelling on the site of a Vazimba village. King Andriamasinavalona later renamed it Antananarivo (“City of the Thousand”) in honor of Andrianjaka’s soldiers. It served as the capital of the Kingdom of Imerina, and King [[Andrianampoinimerina|Andrianampoinimerina]] restored it as the capital of a united kingdom in 1794. It remained the capital after French colonization in 1897 and independence in 1960. The city had 1,274,225 inhabitants at the 2018 census, and its metropolitan area approaches three million. The Presidency, National Assembly, Senate and Supreme Court are located there.

Southernmost of the five major circles of latitude that mark maps of [[Earth]], lying 66°33′51.1″ south of the [[Equator]] by current measurement. Its position shifts with changes in Earth’s [[Axial tilt|axial tilt]], and the circle is currently drifting south at about 14.5 m (48 ft) per year. South of it the Sun is above the horizon for 24 continuous hours at least once a year, a [[Midnight sun|midnight sun]] event, and below the horizon for 24 hours at least once a year. Atmospheric refraction and mirages make part of the midnight sun visible up to about 50 minutes of arc (90 km) north of the circle. No one lives there permanently, although research stations are staffed by seasonal teams. The circle is roughly 16,000 km in circumference, and the area south of it covers about 4% of Earth’s surface.

Northernmost part of mainland [[Antarctica]], projecting about 1,300 km toward [[South America]] and covering 522,000 sq km, about 80% of it under ice. Beneath the ice sheet it consists of a string of bedrock islands, and [[Tierra del Fuego]] lies about 1,000 km away across the [[Drake Passage]]. Edward Bransfield and William Smith first charted part of it on January 30, 1820. Over the past 50 years the warm, moist maritime climate of its northern part has shifted south, causing declines in ice-dependent Adélie penguins, increases in gentoo and chinstrap penguins, and spreading [[Moss|moss]]. Argentina, Chile and the United Kingdom have overlapping claims that none of the countries enforce; the British claim is recognized by Australia, France, New Zealand and Norway, and Argentina has the most bases and personnel on the peninsula.

Continental glacier covering 98% of [[Antarctica]], the largest of Earth’s two current ice sheets. It covers 14 million sq km, averages over 2 km in thickness, and holds 26.5 million cubic km of ice, equivalent to 61% of all fresh water on Earth. It is often divided into the [[Antarctic Peninsula]], the East Antarctic Ice Sheet and the West Antarctic Ice Sheet. The East sheet is over 10 times larger and at higher elevation, so it is less vulnerable to climate change. Ice loss from West Antarctic glaciers such as Thwaites and Pine Island is far greater than the East sheet’s net mass gain in the early 2020s. Net ice loss from Antarctica alone would add about 11 cm (5 in) to global sea level by 2100. If the West Antarctic Ice Sheet collapsed, sea level would rise 3.3 m (10 ft 10 in), or 4.3 m if the ice caps on the mountains also melted, a process estimated to take 2,000 to 13,000 years.

Binary star system and brightest star in the constellation [[Scorpius]]. Its brighter component is a red supergiant, one of the largest stars visible to the naked eye; placed at the center of the [[Solar System]], it would extend out to the [[Asteroid belt|asteroid belt]]. Its mass is estimated at 13 or 15 to 16 times that of the [[Sun]]. The name derives from [[Ancient Greek|Ancient Greek]] “rival to Ares,” for its reddish hue, similar to that of [[Mars]].

Passerine bird family (Thamnophilidae) of subtropical and tropical Central and South America. Its more than 230 species, known as antshrikes, antwrens, antvireos and bushbirds, range from Mexico to Argentina. Antbirds are not closely related to [[Wren|wrens]] or [[Shrike|shrikes]]. Most live in forests and eat mainly insects and other [[Arthropod|arthropods]]. Around 18 species specialize in following swarms of army [[Ant|ants]] to catch invertebrates flushed by the ants. Antbirds are monogamous, defend territories and usually lay two eggs. Both parents share incubation and feeding of the nestlings. Threatened with extinction are 38 species, mainly through habitat loss.

Croatian fascist politician and [[Lawyer|lawyer]]; dictator of the Independent State of Croatia (NDH), a puppet state of [[Nazi Germany]] and Fascist [[Italy]], 1941–45. He founded the Ustaše in Italy in 1929 with the goal of an independent Croatia, and his movement used terrorism, including train bombings and assassinations. The Ustaše were involved in the 1934 assassination of King Alexander of [[Yugoslavia]]. After taking control of the NDH in 1941, his regime imposed anti-Serbian, anti-Semitic and anti-Roma policies that resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Serbs and tens of thousands of Jews and Roma. After the war Pavelić fled to Argentina, where he became a security adviser to [[Juan Perón]]. After an assassination attempt in [[Buenos Aires]], he moved to [[Francoist Spain]], where he was granted political asylum.

One of four extant [[Mammal|mammal]] species of the suborder Vermilingua, which eat mainly ants and termites. The giant anteater (*Myrmecophaga tridactyla*) is about 1.8 m (5 ft 11 in) long including its tail, the silky anteater (*Cyclopes didactylus*) about 35 cm (14 in), and the southern tamandua (*Tamandua tetradactyla*) about 1.2 m (3 ft 11 in). All have elongated snouts, toothless mouths and long, sticky tongues, and they use large foreclaws to break into termite mounds and ant nests. Anteaters are more closely related to [[Sloth|sloths]] than to any other mammal group, and together with sloths they form the order Pilosa. The name is also applied to unrelated animals such as the [[Aardvark|aardvark]], [[Pangolin|pangolins]] and [[Echidna|echidnas]], which share similar features through convergent evolution.

Any [[Ruminant|ruminant]] species of the family [[Bovidae]] other than [[Sheep|sheep]], [[Cattle|cattle]] or [[Goat|goats]]; the term is not a formal taxonomic group. There are 91 species, most of them native to [[Africa]] in about 30 genera, with others in the Arabian Peninsula, South Asia and Central Asia. Antelopes are sometimes misidentified as [[Deer|deer]], to which they are only distantly related. Unlike deer, whose antlers are shed and regrown annually, antelope horns are bone encased in keratin and grow steadily without falling off. The North American [[Pronghorn|pronghorn]] is called the “American antelope” but belongs to a different family, Antilocapridae. The English word first appeared in 1417.

Structure, also called an aerial in British English, that converts alternating electric currents into [[Radio wave|radio waves]] for transmission and converts radio waves back into currents for reception. Antennas are essential components of all [[Radio|radio]] equipment. They may be omnidirectional, radiating equally in all horizontal directions, or directional, concentrating energy in a beam. Their performance is measured by directivity, [[Gain (electronics)|gain]] and bandwidth. The first antennas were built in 1886 by German physicist [[Heinrich Hertz]], who used them to prove the existence of electromagnetic waves predicted by [[James Clerk Maxwell]]’s 1867 theory. From 1895 [[Guglielmo Marconi]] developed antennas practical for long-distance wireless telegraphy, and in 1898 he opened a factory in Chelmsford, England, to manufacture his invention.

Class of water-soluble plant [[Pigment|pigments]] that appear red, pink, purple, blue or black depending on pH. They are flavonoids found in the [[Vacuole|vacuoles]] of flowers, fruits, leaves and roots, and food plants rich in them include blueberries, raspberries and black rice. In flowers and fruits their coloration may attract pollinators and seed dispersers, and they may protect plants against extreme temperatures. Anthocyanins are approved as a food colorant in the European Union but not as a food additive, because they have not been verified as safe. There is little conclusive evidence of effects on human biology or disease.

Australian Labor politician; 31st prime minister of Australia since 2022. Albanese led Labor to victory at the 2022 election and was re-elected in a landslide in 2025. His government created the National Anti-Corruption Commission, updated Australia’s climate targets to reach carbon neutrality by 2050, and introduced a ban on children under sixteen using [[Social media|social media]] platforms. In foreign policy it recognized the State of [[Palestine]] and finalized a free trade agreement with the [[European Union]].

American celebrity chef, author and travel documentarian. After working in professional kitchens, including as executive chef at Brasserie Les Halles in [[Manhattan]], he gained fame with *Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly* (2000). He hosted travel programs including *No Reservations* on the Travel Channel and *Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown* on [[CNN]]. He died by suicide while filming *Parts Unknown* in France.

British Conservative statesman and diplomat; prime minister of the United Kingdom, 1955–57. Eden resigned as foreign secretary in protest at [[Neville Chamberlain]]’s appeasement of [[Benito Mussolini]]’s Fascist Italy, and later served as deputy to [[Winston Churchill]] before succeeding him as prime minister. His reputation as a diplomat was overshadowed by the [[Suez Crisis]] of 1956, when the United States refused to support the Anglo-French military response. Most historians argue that he misjudged the depth of American opposition, and he resigned two months after ending the operation, citing ill health.

Welsh-born actor; knighted in 1993 for services to drama. He was spotted by [[Laurence Olivier]], who invited him to join the Royal National Theatre in 1965, and he won a Laurence Olivier Award for *Pravda* in 1985. He won two [[Academy Awards]] for Best Actor, for playing [[Hannibal Lecter]] in *The Silence of the Lambs* (1991) and for *The Father* (2020). Later work includes the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] films *Thor* and the HBO series *Westworld*.

American actor best known for playing Norman Bates in [[Alfred Hitchcock]]’s *Psycho* (1960). After *Psycho*, which cast him against type, he worked for several years in Europe, including in [[Orson Welles]]’s *The Trial* (1962), before returning to American films. He reprised Norman Bates in three sequels and directed *Psycho III* (1986). In later work he often played troubled or mentally unstable characters.
